unit.title: Si Clauses (Hypothetical)
unit.subtitle: Imagining unreal situations: 'If I were... I would...'

grammar.title: The dream tense: imagine the impossible
grammar.intro: To talk about situations that are unreal or imaginary in the present — things that aren't true but that you like to picture — Spanish pairs the imperfect subjunctive with the conditional. The formula is fixed: si + imperfect subjunctive, then the result in the conditional. Si tuviera dinero, viajaría. Never put the conditional in the si-clause.

sections.heading: si + imperfect subjunctive → conditional
sections.body: This is the mirror of the real conditional you learned in unit 13. Here the condition is imaginary, so the si-clause takes the imperfect subjunctive and the result takes the conditional:
conj: Si fuera rico, compraría una casa.
Si ganara la lotería, dejaría de trabajar.

ex.en: If I had money, I'd travel the world.
If I were you, I wouldn't do it.

sections.heading: Asking 'what would you do if...?'
sections.body: A very common pattern flips the order and asks a question. The conditional leads, and the si clause with the imperfect subjunctive follows:

ex.en: What would you do if you won the lottery?
Where would you go if you could travel for free?

sections.heading: Keep each half in its own mood
sections.body: The two classic slips: putting the conditional after si, or repeating the subjunctive in the result. Each half has exactly one job:

takeaways: Hypothetical: si + imperfect subjunctive, result in the conditional.
Si tuviera dinero, viajaría · Si fuera rico, compraría una casa.
Question form: ¿Qué harías si ganaras la lotería?
Never 'si tendría' (use si tuviera) and never a subjunctive result (use viajaría).

mistakes.why: The si-clause takes the imperfect subjunctive, not the conditional: tuviera.
The result clause must be the conditional (viajaría), not another subjunctive.

mistakes.w: Si fuera rico, compro una casa.
mistakes.r: Si fuera rico, compraría una casa.
mistakes.why: An unreal condition needs the conditional in the result, not the present.

exercises.prompt: Si ___ dinero, viajaría por el mundo.
exercises.prompt_en: If I had money, I'd travel the world.
exercises.no: The unreal si-clause needs the imperfect subjunctive: “si tuviera”.

exercises.prompt: Si fuera rico, ___ una casa grande.
exercises.prompt_en: If I were rich, I'd buy a big house.
exercises.ok: ¡Exacto! El resultado va en condicional: compraría.
exercises.no: The result of an unreal condition takes the conditional: “compraría”.

exercises.prompt: Build: “What would you do if you won the lottery?”
exercises.no: “¿Qué harías si ganaras la lotería?” — conditional + si + imperfect subjunctive.

exercises.prompt: Si fuera tú, no lo ___. (hacer, yo)
exercises.prompt_en: If I were you, I wouldn't do it.
exercises.hint: The result clause is conditional: hacer → har- + ía.
exercises.no: The result takes the conditional: “no lo haría”.

exercises.prompt: Match each hypothetical si-clause to its conditional result.

exercises.tts: Si fuera rico, compraría una casa.
accepted: si fuera rico compraria una casa
si fuera rico, compraria una casa
exercises.translation: If I were rich, I'd buy a house.
exercises.no: It was: “Si fuera rico, compraría una casa.” (If I were rich, I'd buy a house.)

exercises.scenario: Daydreaming with a friend about winning big 💰
